chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq al-Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), concerning a woman who was divorced and had reached an advanced age, who experienced one period of menstruation, then her menstruation ceased.
He said: She observes the waiting period by that one menstruation and two following months, for she has become menopausal (lost hope of menstruation).

Therefore, the correct interpretation of this report is to restrict it to a woman who had become menopausal after experiencing one period of menstruation; for after that menstruation passes, she observes the waiting period of two months, in accordance with what the first report contained.

key_terms.يَئِسَتْ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ: became menopausal / lost hope of menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a menopausal woman who had one period before divorce?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve the juristic debate regarding the 'iddah of a menopausal woman (al-mu'assamah) who experiences a single menstruation before her periods cease. By specifying that the waiting period comprises that one menstruation followed by two months, the Imam clarifies the application of the Quranic verse on menopause, ensuring the ruling accounts for the residual sign of fertility before finalizing the divorce's legal effects.
